MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Roman numeral stands for 8? (1 mark)
   A. IIII
   B. VIII
   C. VIIII
   D. VX

2. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 6,092? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 9
   C. 10
   D. 90

3. How many factors does 28 have? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 6
   C. 5
   D. 8

4. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 6,478 + 2,355? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

5. Estimate 1,743 + 6,286 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 8,129
   B. 8,040
   C. 8,020
   D. 8,030

6. Why can we add 3,875 + 2,450 in either order? (1 mark)
   A. The answer is always the bigger number
   B. The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order
   C. The sum changes when the order changes
   D. Only the bigger number can go first

7. When we subtract 1,236 from 4,000, what do we do first? (1 mark)
   A. Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds
   B. Add 1,236 to 4,000
   C. Subtract the thousands digits only
   D. Take the smaller digit from the bigger digit in each column

8. A stadium seats 9,000 people. If 6,450 seats are taken, how many seats are empty? (1 mark)
   A. 2,650 seats
   B. 2,540 seats
   C. 3,450 seats
   D. 2,550 seats

9. Which number is in the 9 times table? (1 mark)
   A. 71
   B. 74
   C. 72
   D. 75

10. What is 99 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 9,900
   B. 199
   C. 990
   D. 99,000

11. Work out 45 × 18. (1 mark)
   A. 820
   B. 405
   C. 800
   D. 810

12. What is 450 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 5 remainder 50
   B. 4 remainder 50
   C. 45
   D. 4 remainder 5

13. What is 300 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 300
   B. 3
   C. 30
   D. 4

14. 45 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 6 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 9
   C. 8
   D. 7

15. Change 17/5 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 2 3/5
   B. 3 3/5
   C. 3 2/5
   D. 4 2/5

16. What is 3/5 of 25? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 15
   C. 5
   D. 20

17. Change 25/6 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1 4/6
   B. 4 2/6
   C. 5 1/6
   D. 4 1/6

18. Which is the largest number: 0.9, 0.09, 0.85, 0.099? (1 mark)
   A. 0.09
   B. 0.85
   C. 0.9
   D. 0.099

19. A hundred square has 82 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.082
   B. 8.2
   C. 0.82
   D. 82

20. In the number 13.42, the digit 2 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tens
   C. Tenths
   D. Hundredths

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A shop buys 24 boxes of pencils. Each box has 36 pencils. (a) Estimate the number of pencils by rounding to the nearest ten. (b) Work out the exact number of pencils. (5 marks)

22. State whether 1,468 and 3,975 are even or odd. Give a reason for each. (3 marks)

23. A school tank held 8,500 litres of water. The school used 3,275 litres in the first week and 1,850 litres in the second week. How much water is left? Check your answer. (5 marks)

24. What number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? Explain how you found it. (3 marks)

25. List all the factors of 36. (3 marks)

26. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. Show how you regroup. (3 marks)

27. Write 7,206 in expanded form. (2 marks)

28. 45 eggs are packed in trays that hold 6 eggs each. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? Explain. (3 marks)

29. Divide 47 by 5. Check your answer using multiplication and addition. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — VIII
   8 is written VIII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

2. D — 90
   The digit 9 is in the tens place, so its total value is 9 × 10 = 90.

3. B — 6
   The factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. There are 6 of them.

4. B — 2
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 6,478 + 2,355 needs 2 regroupings.

5. D — 8,030
   1,743 rounds to 1,740 and 6,286 rounds to 6,290. 1,740 + 6,290 = 8,030.

6. B — The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order
   Addition can be done in any order: 3,875 + 2,450 = 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

7. A — Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds
   The ones digit 0 is smaller than 6 and the tens and hundreds are zeros, so we borrow from the thousands.

8. D — 2,550 seats
   Subtract 9,000 − 6,450 = 2,550. Check by adding: 2,550 + 6,450 = 9,000.

9. C — 72
   9 × 8 = 72. The digits of a multiple of 9 add up to 9: 7 + 2 = 9.

10. A — 9,900
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 99 × 100 = 9,900.

11. D — 810
   45 × 8 = 360 and 45 × 10 = 450. 360 + 450 = 810.

12. B — 4 remainder 50
   4 × 100 = 400 and 450 − 400 = 50. So 450 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 50.

13. B — 3
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 300 ÷ 100 = 3.

14. C — 8
   45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. The 3 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

15. C — 3 2/5
   17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 2/5, so 17/5 = 3 2/5.

16. B — 15
   25 ÷ 5 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/5 of 25 is 15.

17. D — 4 1/6
   25 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/6, so 25/6 = 4 1/6.

18. C — 0.9
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 0.9.

19. C — 0.82
   82 out of 100 squares is 82/100 = 0.82.

20. D — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 13.42 the digit 2 is in the hundredths place.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 20 × 40 = 800 (b) 864 pencils
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 800, 2 marks for 36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720, 1 mark for 864.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,468 is even because it ends in 8. 3,975 is odd because it ends in 5.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct classification with a reason (2 marks) and 1 mark for referring to the ones digit.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: 3,375 litres
   Working / marking points: 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225 (2 marks); 5,225 − 1,850 = 3,375 (2 marks); check by adding 3,375 + 1,850 + 3,275 = 8,500 (1 mark).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,318. Subtract 5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using subtraction, 1 mark for the working, 1 mark for the answer 2,318.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36
   Working / marking points: Pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 3 marks for all nine factors, 2 marks for seven or eight, 1 mark for at least five.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,764
   Working / marking points: Borrow from the thousands so the number is 3 thousands 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones (1 mark). 10 − 6 = 4, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 2 = 7, 3 − 1 = 2 (1 mark). Answer 2,764 (1 mark).

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: 7,000 + 200 + 6
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7,000 and 200; 1 mark for 6 ones with no tens.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 trays
   Working / marking points: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3 (1 mark). Seven trays are full (1 mark). The 3 left-over eggs need another tray, so 8 trays (1 mark).

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9, 1 mark for remainder 2, 1 mark for the check.
